assumptions: 1. THE WIRING IS THE SUITE'S. The verbs take the mapping an installation wires in (the one the receiver is given), with the authority's issue of a run and, when the installation has its own, a containment group. Nothing serves the ledger to a CLI process yet (the authority's socket is VELDO-0323's), so on a host with an installation the CLI says the space ledger is not reachable, the wrapper runs its command unchanged and record and event record nothing. NOT PROVEN HERE: one wrapped run from a shell against a running authority.

2. THE RUN'S END FOR A COMMAND THAT LEFT A PROCESS IS DRIVEN BY THE SUITE. In production the run's supervisor makes it, by a process that follows it, with the wiring that process resolves for itself; until VELDO-0323 that process reaches no ledger, sends nothing, and the run's items and hold stay for reconcile. The suite calls the same function (_space_ended) in its own process. The few lines in the supervisor that resolve a wiring and hand over have no row.

3. THE CONTAINMENT GROUP IS A STAND-IN IN EVERY ROW BUT ONE. Suite 151 runs inside the gate's confinement, which has no user manager. Row fix3/the-house-group makes the house's own scope where the host has a manager (seen green on the build host in the first fix round; not in round 2, where the run's end there waits for other sessions' unread processes) and stands down by name where it has none. What the supervisor sees and what the process table shows are the kernel's in every row. The worktree the command runs in is declared by the suite (VELDO-0302, 0311); the two checks of a switch to act (VELDO-0332, 0339) are stand-ins that allow; free space is a function of the suite; the process table the rules of Signal read is a folder with no entry.
4. THE DOCKER ENGINE IS A STAND-IN that holds what a row plants and stops and removes one named object. No row asks a real engine.
5. THE DECLARED FALSIFIER OF AC3 DOES NOT MAKE AN ITEM. With the CLI's check removed the Ledger still refuses the path, by another name. The row is red on the name.

6. THE EVENT VERB RECORDS NOTHING YET. The Ledger's event command is VELDO-0323's (released: VELDO-0335); until then the answer is space_no_command:space_event, said by the verb, and nothing becomes due. VELDO-0314's footprint now names the spool module and the CLI, so that the event verb can spool.

7. UNREAD PROCESSES HOLD THE RUN (fix round 2, the lead's decision; the first round's bound is gone). A process whose environment cannot be read and that started at or after the run's supervisor holds the run, whatever its uid and whatever started it. Left out, by the kernel's facts alone: one that started before the run and is no descendant and no group member; and kernel threads. NOT SEEN: a process from before the run that replaced its own program afterwards. CONSEQUENCE: on a host without the process reader (VELDO-0344) a run ends only when every such process has exited; on the build host (423 unread processes, 190 younger than 20 minutes, new ones every second) no wrapped run ends, and suite 151 is green only in a process table of its own. With the reader used, a process with a whole block and the kernel's start time is read and rule 4 judges it by its files; the reader prints no environment, so its label is still not read. NOT PROVEN HERE: the installed reader itself (the row's reader is a stand-in for the probe's reader_read), and a process of another uid (the row's unread processes are the owner's own, made not dumpable).

8. THE LEDGER'S OWN RULE STILL LETS space-observer DECLARE SESSION SCRATCH AT ANY PATH INSIDE A ROOT (control_space.permit). The CLI's record verb no longer reaches it, and no other verb does. Narrowing the rule needs a ticket whose footprint holds control_space.py.

9. AC1 SAYS THE END IS MADE BEFORE THE WRAPPER EXITS. That holds for a run whose group has ended when the command exits. For a command that left a process the lead's decision replaces it: the wrapper exits with the status and the end follows. The criterion's text is the design's and was not edited.
10. NOT RUN BY THE BUILDER: ./scripts/verify.sh and the heavy suites.
